Examination Readiness & Presentation
Compliance Instructions
Applicable EduQual Qualifications: EduQual Level 3 to 6 Diploma Qualifications
Document Owner: Academic Operations Center
Center Name: Al Nafi International College
Dated: 9th January, 2026
1. Purpose and Regulatory Alignment
These instructions establish the minimum mandatory preparation standards for students
appearing in EduQual Level 3, 4, 5, and 6 assessments.
The objective is to ensure that:
● Learning outcomes are fully met and demonstrable
● Assessments align with EduQual and Ofqual expectations
● Submissions reflect industry readiness and employer-aligned competence
● Academic integrity is preserved while responsibly leveraging AI as a tool
This framework reflects:
● EduQual assessment principles
● Ofqual conditions of recognition
● EduQual & RQF level descriptors
● Current global industry practices
2. Mandatory Preparation Requirements (Non-Negotiable)
Every student MUST ensure the following are fully prepared for each selected topic, where
applicable.
2.1 Conceptual and Theoretical Readiness
Students must demonstrate:
● Clear understanding of core concepts, terminology, and frameworks
● Ability to explain why a solution exists, not just what it is

● Alignment of explanations with the RQF level depth (increasing complexity from Level 3

Superficial explanations or memorized definitions are insufficient.
2.2 Design & Architecture Artifacts (Mandatory Where Applicable)
For every topic, students MUST be able to independently explain and defend the following
artifacts:
● System Architecture Diagrams
● Network Diagrams
● Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)
● Process Flow / Workflow Diagrams
● Security Architecture Diagrams
● Cloud / Hybrid / On-Prem Architecture Designs
Requirements:
● Diagrams must be logically consistent
● Components must be correctly placed and justified
● Data movement, trust boundaries, and dependencies must be clearly explained
● The student must be able to modify or redesign the architecture live during Q&A
Pre-made diagrams without understanding will be penalized.
2.3 Implementation & Demonstration Capability
Students must be able to demonstrate:
● How the solution works end-to-end
● How components interact in real scenarios
● How the design would be implemented in practice
This includes:
● Configuration logic
● Deployment flow
● Operational behavior
● Failure and recovery scenarios
● Scalability and security considerations
Live demos, walkthroughs, or simulated demonstrations may be required depending on the
topic and level.

2.4 Policies, Procedures, and Governance (Where Applicable)
Students must prepare and be able to justify:
● Policies (what must be followed and why)
● Procedures (how things are executed step-by-step)
● Standards and controls aligned with industry frameworks
● Compliance, risk, and governance considerations
At higher RQF levels (5–6), students must show:
● Decision-making rationale
● Trade-off analysis
● Alignment with regulatory and organizational objectives
3. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Allowed and Restricted Areas
3.1 Permitted Use of AI (Explicitly Allowed)
AI may be used for:
● Writing code
● Generating scripts
● Producing configuration samples
● Assisting with documentation drafts
● Demonstrating how a solution operates
This reflects modern industry reality where AI-assisted development is standard practice.
3.2 Restricted Use of AI (Strictly Evaluated)
AI MUST NOT replace:
● Student understanding
● Student reasoning
● Student design thinking
● Student explanation
● Student problem-solving during Q&A
All of the following are individually evaluated:
● Creativity

● Alignment with regulatory and organizational objectives

● Logical flow
● Technical justification
● Real-world reasoning
● Ability to defend decisions verbally
AI usage is assessed as a tool, not as a substitute for competence.
4. Evaluation Framework Used During the Exam
All presentations and interviews are evaluated strictly using the following structure.
4.1 Presentation Evaluation (50% | Total Marks: 25)
Final Evaluation Report Structure
Presentation Title:
Presenter:
Diploma:
1. Does the Presentation Meet the Examination Requirements?
● Observations from the Presentation
● Topics Covered
● Missing Key Requirements
● Conclusion
2. Is AI Likely Used in the Creation of This Presentation?
● Analysis
● Possible AI Assistance
● Human-Created Aspects
● Conclusion
3. Areas for Improvement
(A) Technical Depth & Exam Alignment
(B) Visuals & Presentation Quality

Scoring Criteria
Criteria Weightage Evaluation Focus
Content Mastery 20% Depth, accuracy, and clarity
Organization 20% Logical flow and structure
Presentation Skills 20% Confidence, articulation, defense
Use of Visuals 20% Diagrams, clarity, relevance
Usage of AI Tools 20% Responsible, transparent, appropriate
Total: 25 Marks
4.2 Q&A / Interview Evaluation (50% | Total Marks: 25)
Students must demonstrate:
● Real-time reasoning
● Design defense
● Scenario handling
● Employer-style questioning readiness
A minimum of 10 structured questions may be asked, covering:
● Architecture decisions
● Failure scenarios
● Security implications
● Performance trade-offs
● Real-world deployment challenges
5. Performance Expectations by RQF Level
● RQF Level 3: Foundational understanding and basic demonstrations
● RQF Level 4: Applied knowledge with structured designs
● RQF Level 5: Analytical thinking, optimization, and justification
● RQF Level 6: Strategic architecture, risk-based decisions, and enterprise alignment
Expectations increase significantly with each level.

6. Final Verdict and Recommendations
Final outcomes include:
● Strengths
● Areas needing attention
● Clear recommendation
● Final score out of 50
● Performance level classification
Passing requires both technical competence and demonstrable understanding.
7. Institutional Position
Al Nafi International College evaluates:
● Skills, not templates
● Understanding, not memorization
● Readiness for employment, not academic theory alone
Students are expected to perform as entry-level to mid-level professionals, depending on the
RQF level.
8. Closing Statement
This instruction set exists to:
● Protect qualification integrity
● Align education with real-world demand
● Ensure students graduate with defensible, employable skills
Students are encouraged to prepare thoroughly, think critically, and present confidently.
The assessment process is rigorous by design and fair by principle.

Exam Topic for Oral Presentation
EduQual Level 6
Code: ANPP-OP
Version: 0.1

Student Name Jawad Ahmad

Enterprise Capstone Project 21
Qualification
Diploma in AIOPS
Primary Core Integration Framework (CIF)
Discipline
E-Commerce & Digital Trade (Online Marketplaces,
Cross-Border Commerce, Digital Supply Networks and
Intelligent Commerce Platforms)
Primary Assessment Domain
The primary purpose of this Enterprise Capstone Project is to assess the student's ability to
design, develop, deploy, demonstrate, and defend an Enterprise Cross-Border Digital
Commerce Platform capable of managing global customers, merchants, products, inventory,
intelligent pricing, international orders, digital payments (simulated), logistics integration,
AI-assisted demand forecasting, and executive business intelligence.
Although students will use Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, DevSecOps, Infrastructure
as Code, Monitoring, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Databases, APIs, Automation, and
Data Analytics throughout the project, these technologies are supporting implementation
technologies. The primary assessment focuses on Enterprise Digital Commerce,
Cross-Border Trade, Marketplace Engineering, Order Management, Supply Chain
Visibility, Customer Experience Management, AI-assisted Business Analytics, and
Enterprise Commerce Operations.
This project shall execute successfully on a laptop containing 8–16 GB RAM.

Industry Sector
Global E-Commerce and Digital Trade
Client
GlobalCommerce Marketplace International
(Fictional Organisation for Assessment Purposes)
Project Title
Design and Implementation of an Enterprise
Cross-Border Digital Commerce Platform for Marketplace
Management, Intelligent Inventory Optimization,
AI-Assisted Demand Forecasting, International Order
Processing, Logistics Visibility, and Executive Commerce
Analytics
1. Project Background
GlobalCommerce Marketplace International operates one of the world's fastest-growing
cross-border digital marketplaces connecting buyers, sellers, logistics providers, and fulfilment
centres across multiple countries.
The organisation manages:

● Online Marketplace
● Merchant Management
● Product Catalogue
● Inventory Management
● Customer Accounts
● Order Management
● International Shipping
● Warehouse Operations
● Business Intelligence Platform
● Customer Service Operations
The organisation processes more than 5 million simulated customer transactions daily.
Current operations rely on multiple disconnected systems responsible for inventory, customer
management, payments, shipping, merchant onboarding, analytics, and reporting.
As business expands internationally, management requires a centralized enterprise platform
capable of improving operational visibility, customer experience, intelligent forecasting, and
executive decision-making.
The organisation has appointed your consulting company to design and implement a
proof-of-concept Enterprise Digital Commerce Platform.
The completed solution should demonstrate how Artificial Intelligence, enterprise software
engineering, cloud-native platforms, and intelligent analytics improve global digital commerce.
2. Business Problem
GlobalCommerce currently manages products, customers, merchants, warehouses, logistics,
inventory, pricing, and analytics using multiple independent software platforms.
This results in:
● Poor inventory visibility.
● Delayed order fulfilment.
● Overstocking.
● Stock shortages.
● Inefficient merchant onboarding.
● Limited executive reporting.

● Inconsistent customer experience.
Executive management requires an Enterprise Digital Commerce Platform capable of
integrating marketplace operations, intelligent inventory forecasting, logistics tracking, customer
management, AI-assisted demand forecasting, and executive dashboards.
The proposed solution should demonstrate how enterprise software engineering improves
operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and business intelligence.
3. Project Objective
Design, develop, deploy, and demonstrate an Enterprise Cross-Border Digital Commerce
Platform capable of supporting simulated international marketplace operations.
The completed solution shall demonstrate:
● Marketplace Management
● Merchant Management
● Product Management
● Inventory Management
● Warehouse Management
● International Order Processing
● Logistics Monitoring
● AI-assisted Demand Forecasting
● Executive Dashboards
● Enterprise Monitoring
● Professional Documentation
Only simulated customers, products, payments, logistics, and inventory shall be used.
4. Laptop Resource Constraint
The project shall execute comfortably on:
● Minimum RAM: 8 GB

● Recommended RAM: 16 GB
● Docker Compose deployment
● PostgreSQL database
● Lightweight AI models
● Small simulated datasets
● No GPU required
● Kubernetes optional using K3s or Kind
● No Apache Spark
● No distributed clusters
● No locally hosted LLMs
5. Required Functional Modules
Module 1 – Marketplace and Merchant Management
Platform
Develop a centralized marketplace platform.
The platform shall:
● Register merchants.
● Register customers.
● Manage merchant verification.
● Manage customer accounts.
● Maintain marketplace statistics.
● Generate merchant reports.
● Display operational dashboards.
● Manage account status.
Students shall explain how marketplace management improves scalability and customer trust.
Module 2 – Product, Inventory and Warehouse
Management Platform

Develop an inventory management system.
The platform shall:
● Register products.
● Manage product categories.
● Track warehouse inventory.
● Record stock movement.
● Monitor stock levels.
● Generate inventory reports.
● Display warehouse dashboards.
● Produce inventory analytics.
Students shall explain how intelligent inventory management supports global commerce.
Module 3 – International Order and Logistics
Management Platform
Develop an order management platform.
The platform shall:
● Process simulated customer orders.
● Track order lifecycle.
● Assign warehouse fulfilment.
● Simulate shipment creation.
● Track shipment status.
● Generate delivery reports.
● Display logistics dashboards.
● Record operational history.
Students shall explain how integrated logistics improve customer satisfaction and operational
efficiency.
Module 4 – AI-Assisted Demand Forecasting Platform
Develop a lightweight Artificial Intelligence platform.

The platform shall:
● Import historical sales datasets.
● Perform data preprocessing.
● Train a lightweight forecasting model.
● Predict future product demand.
● Predict stock shortages.
● Recommend inventory replenishment.
● Generate forecasting reports.
● Display confidence scores.
Students shall explain how Artificial Intelligence supports supply chain planning while requiring
business validation before operational implementation.
Module 5 – Executive Commerce Intelligence Dashboard
Develop an executive dashboard displaying:
● Marketplace performance.
● Active merchants.
● Customer registrations.
● Inventory availability.
● Warehouse utilisation.
● Order volume.
● Shipping performance.
● Demand forecasts.
● Financial KPIs.
● Executive reports.
Students shall explain how executive dashboards improve strategic business decision-making.
6. Primary Learning Outcomes
Students should be able to:
● Design enterprise digital commerce platforms.

● Develop marketplace management systems.
● Build inventory management applications.
● Design warehouse operations software.
● Develop AI forecasting models.
● Build REST APIs.
● Develop executive dashboards.
● Deploy lightweight enterprise software.
● Produce professional technical documentation.
● Defend architectural decisions during viva voce assessment.
7. Standard Open-Source Technology
Stack
Programming Language
● Python
Backend Development
● FastAPI
Frontend Development
● React
Database
● PostgreSQL
Cache
● Redis

Machine Learning
● Scikit-learn
● Prophet
● Pandas
● NumPy
Data Visualisation
● Plotly
● Matplotlib
API Documentation
● OpenAPI
● Swagger UI
Workflow Automation
● Apache Airflow (optional)
Search Engine
● OpenSearch
Authentication
● Keycloak (optional)
● FastAPI JWT Authentication
Containerisation
● Docker
● Docker Compose
Optional Lightweight Kubernetes

● K3s
● Kind
Monitoring
● Prometheus
● Grafana
Logging
● Loki
Security
● Trivy
● Semgrep
● Open Policy Agent
API Testing
● Bruno
● Postman
Version Control
● Git
● GitHub
Documentation
● Markdown
● MkDocs
Architecture
● Draw.io
● PlantUML

● Mermaid
8. Mandatory Architecture and
Engineering Deliverables
Students shall prepare and explain:
1. Enterprise Digital Commerce Architecture Diagram.
2. High-Level Solution Architecture Diagram.
3. Detailed System Architecture Diagram.
4. Marketplace Management Architecture Diagram.
5. Inventory Management Architecture Diagram.
6. Warehouse Management Architecture Diagram.
7. Logistics Management Architecture Diagram.
8. AI Demand Forecasting Architecture Diagram.
9. Enterprise Network Architecture Diagram.
10. Network Flow Diagram.
11. Data Flow Diagram (Level 0).
12. Data Flow Diagram (Level 1).
13. Marketplace Workflow Diagram.
14. Order Fulfilment Workflow Diagram.
15. Demand Forecasting Workflow Diagram.
16. Logistics Workflow Diagram.
17. Database Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD).
18. Sequence Diagram illustrating customer registration, product ordering, inventory
validation, shipment processing, AI demand forecasting, and executive reporting.
All diagrams shall be professionally prepared and explained during both the presentation and
the viva voce examination.
9. Applicable International Standards and
Frameworks

The proposed solution shall demonstrate consideration of:
● GS1 Global Standards (Product Identification and Supply Chains)
● ISO 8000 – Data Quality
● ISO 9001 – Quality Management Systems
● ISO 28000 – Supply Chain Security Management
● ISO/IEC 27001 – Information Security Management Systems
● ISO/IEC 27017 – Cloud Security
● ISO/IEC 27018 – Protection of Personal Data in the Cloud
● ISO/IEC 42001 – Artificial Intelligence Management Systems
● NIST AI Risk Management Framework
● NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
● OWASP Top 10
● OWASP API Security Top 10
● CIS Critical Security Controls
● COBIT 2019
● ITIL 4
Students shall explain how these standards improve data quality, supply chain security,
cybersecurity, AI governance, privacy, enterprise operations, and digital commerce.
10. Examination Format
Stage 1 – Enterprise Solution Presentation (15–20
Minutes)
Students shall present:
● Client background.
● Business problem.
● Project objectives.
● Digital commerce domain overview.
● Enterprise architecture.
● Marketplace architecture.
● Inventory architecture.
● Logistics architecture.
● AI forecasting architecture.

● Enterprise network architecture.
● Network Flow Diagram.
● Data Flow Diagrams.
● Database design.
● Technology stack.
● Applicable standards and frameworks.
● Expected business outcomes.
● Future enhancements.
Stage 2 – Live Project Demonstration and GitHub Review
(5–10 Minutes)
Students shall demonstrate:
● GitHub repository.
● Source code walkthrough.
● Marketplace Management Platform.
● Product and Inventory Management Platform.
● Order Management Platform.
● AI Demand Forecasting Platform.
● Executive Dashboard.
● Docker Compose deployment.
● API testing.
● Database queries.
● Monitoring dashboard.
● Test execution summary.
The project must execute successfully on a standard student laptop with 8–16 GB RAM.
Stage 3 – Professional Technical Interview and Viva Voce
(30–40 Minutes)
Questions may cover:
● Enterprise marketplace architecture.
● Inventory optimisation.

● Warehouse management.
● Cross-border commerce.
● Digital logistics.
● Demand forecasting.
● REST API design.
● FastAPI.
● PostgreSQL.
● Docker Compose.
● Prometheus and Grafana.
● JWT authentication.
● Enterprise monitoring.
● AI governance.
● Cybersecurity.
● International standards.
● Performance optimisation for laptop environments.
● Future developments in digital commerce.
Scenario-based questions may require students to redesign the platform to support a global
marketplace with multiple currencies, regional warehouses, AI-driven pricing, international
fulfilment centres, and millions of simulated daily transactions while maintaining scalability,
reliability, and security.
11. GitHub Repository Requirements
The GitHub repository shall include:
● Complete source code.
● FastAPI backend.
● React frontend.
● PostgreSQL database schema.
● Marketplace management module.
● Product and inventory management module.
● Order processing module.
● Logistics simulation module.
● AI demand forecasting module.
● Dockerfile.
● Docker Compose configuration.
● Optional lightweight Kubernetes manifests.

● Prometheus and Grafana configuration.
● Architecture diagrams.
● Database ERD.
● API documentation.
● Installation Guide.
● Deployment Guide.
● User Guide.
● Administrator Guide.
● Unit and integration test reports.
● AI model evaluation report.
● Security scan reports from Trivy and Semgrep.
● API testing collection (Bruno or Postman).
● A comprehensive README.md describing the project objectives, architecture,
implementation methodology, deployment process, laptop hardware requirements, assumptions,
limitations, testing methodology, scalability considerations, and recommendations for future
enhancements.
12. Note for Students
This Enterprise Capstone Project has been designed to assess the knowledge and practical
skills acquired throughout the Diploma in AIOPS.
Students are strongly encouraged to complete as many practical laboratories as possible from
Ar Razzaq Part 1 and Ar Razzaq Part 2 before attempting the final assessment.
Access to the Ar Razzaq laboratories requires maintaining an active membership in the
Diploma in AIOPS. Completion of these laboratories is recommended but not mandatory for
eligibility to undertake the final examination.
Students who complete the laboratories will gain substantial practical experience in Python,
FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, APIs, monitoring, DevSecOps, Artificial Intelligence,
enterprise software engineering, cloud-native application development, and modern system
architecture. This experience is expected to significantly improve their ability to complete the
capstone project, deliver a professional presentation, demonstrate a working enterprise digital
commerce platform, and confidently defend their technical and architectural decisions during the
viva voce examination.
